chunks: Al-Hasan ibn Mahbub from Khalid ibn Jarir from Abu al-Rabii said:

Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) said: 'Indeed, Allah, the Mighty and Majestic, forbade wine itself, so its little and much is forbidden, just as He forbade the carcass, blood, and meat of the pig. And the Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him and his family) forbade drink from every intoxicant, and whatever the Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him and his family) forbade, Allah, the Mighty and Majestic, has forbidden.'
ai.seo_question: What is the relationship between the prohibition of wine and other intoxicants in Shia jurisprudence?
ai.summary: Imam al-Sadiq (peace be upon him) establishes the principle of *tawatur* (convergence) between divine prohibition and prophetic tradition, asserting that the Prophet’s ban on all intoxicants (*khamr*) carries the same weight as Allah’s explicit decree. This hadith underscores the Shia jurisprudential view that the Sunnah is not merely explanatory but constitutive of the Sharia, linking the specific prohibition of wine to the broader category of all *muskir* (intoxicants).
